subject: IAM evidence request: SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC — Galileo Medical
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@galileo-med.com>
Cc: Galile0 Security <security@galileo-med.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: IAM evidence request: SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC — Galileo Medical

Hi Oliver — great to meet today. Thanks for taking the time to walk through your integration goals and compliance needs. Per our call, I wanted to capture the next steps and share the IAM artifacts you asked for.

Recap / action items:
- You: share vendor security questionnaire (VSA) and any specific evidence IDs you need by EOD Friday.
- Me: provide SSO (SAML) configuration details, SCIM provisioning overview, admin RBAC matrix, and SOC 2 evidence summary.
- Aditya (cc): will share the SCIM schema and example provisioning payloads.

Quick answers to the questions you flagged on the call:
- SOC 2: Redwood completed Type II in 2026; summary attached and we can provide the full report under an NDA.
- SSO/SAML: we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, metadata XML + ACS URL + cert.
- SCIM: SCIM v2 supported for user provisioning/deprovisioning; attribute mapping customizable.
- RBAC/Admin controls: granular roles (Org Admin, Billing Admin, App Admin, Read-Only) and audit logs for all role changes.

Attachments (stubs): redwood_sso-config-stub.pdf, redwood_scim-overview.pdf, soc2-summary-2026.pdf

Please confirm what specific artifacts from the questionnaire you want as separate documents (e.g., SAML metadata XML, SCIM sample payloads, audit log retention policy). I can route any NDA requests to our legal team.

Next meeting: are you available Mon 4/19 at 10am PT for a short technical handoff with your SRE/security engineer?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: IAM evidence request: SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC — Galileo Medical

Hi Oliver — quick technical notes and attached sample payloads.

Answers:
- SCIM deprovisioning: when a user is marked inactive via SCIM (active=false), our platform revokes API tokens and invalidates sessions within 15 seconds under normal operating conditions; session revocation is propagated to all active services. (We record the event in audit logs.)

Attached (stubs):
- redwood_scim-overview.pdf (includes sample SCIM PATCH/PUT payloads and attribute mapping)
- redwood_sso-config-stub.pdf (SAML metadata endpoints + cert thumbprint)

SCIM notes (summary):
- SCIM v2 endpoint: https://api.redwoodinference.com/v2/scim/Users
- Supports bulk and incremental provisioning, with retry logic and idempotency keys.
- Attributes: userName, name.familyName, name.givenName, emails[type=work], active, groups (for role mapping).

RBAC notes:
- Built-in roles: Org Admin, Billing Admin, App Admin, Developer, Read-Only.
- Custom role creation supported via Console API; role change events appear in audit log with actor, timestamp, and before/after.

If Galileo wants, we can produce a minimal signed metadata XML and sample SCIM request in the shared Drive for your SRE to import.

--
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com

Hi Marissa / Aditya — thanks for the quick response and detail. A few follow-ups from the security review: 

1) Please upload the SOC 2 scope page and auditor name to the shared Drive link (we have Procure access will request the full report under NDA).
2) We need the SAML metadata XML file and the public cert (separate files) so our IdP team can import them into Okta.
3) For SCIM, can you provide a short note on rate limits and retries (typical TPS and backoff behavior)?
4) Confirm retention for audit logs (how long are role-change/SSO events retained in logs?).

If you can provide the SAML metadata + cert and a short SOC 2 scope PDF by EOD Friday, we can move forward with the procurement checklist.

Thanks,
Simon Lee
